skill.description: Guidance for advanced Git workflows, including interactive rebase, conflict resolution, branch maintenance, history recovery, and troubleshooting.

security_audit.summary: The static alerts are primarily false positives from Markdown examples and ordinary Git helper commands. One medium-confidence usability risk remains: the conflict helper can apply “ours” or “theirs” changes immediately after menu selection. No evidence of prompt injection, credential exfiltration, or malicious network activity was found.

remediation.issue: Conflict resolution applies file changes immediately after a menu choice.
remediation.suggestion: Show the affected files and require an explicit confirmation before running checkout and add operations.

remediation.issue: Branch cleanup examples and helper commands can delete local branches.
remediation.suggestion: Retain the confirmation prompt and replace xargs examples with null-delimited, option-terminated handling where practical.

remediation.issue: SSH troubleshooting uses a default private-key filename.
remediation.suggestion: Explain that users should select the intended key path and avoid loading keys they do not control.

content.value_statement: Complex Git operations can damage history or lose work when performed without a clear plan. This skill provides structured guidance for rebasing, resolving conflicts, managing branches, and recovering commits.
actual_capabilities: Explains interactive rebase actions for cleaning and reorganizing commits.
Provides conflict-resolution patterns for common source-code changes.
Guides Git bisect workflows for locating a regression.
Describes branch cleanup, Git Flow, and trunk-based development strategies.
Explains reflog-based recovery after resets, rebases, or deleted commits.
Includes a local Bash helper for branch, conflict, backup, and stash tasks.
limitations: It provides guidance and does not replace repository-specific review or backups.
Some operations rewrite history and require coordination before pushing shared branches.
The helper script is Bash-specific and requires Git and related local tools.
Examples use placeholders and must be adapted to the actual repository.

use_cases.title: Clean a feature branch
use_cases.description: Reorganize local commits before opening a pull request while preserving a backup branch.

use_cases.title: Resolve a difficult merge
use_cases.description: Compare competing changes and choose a safe, testable conflict-resolution approach.

use_cases.title: Recover lost work
use_cases.description: Use reflog guidance to locate and restore a commit after an accidental reset or rebase.

prompt_templates.title: Beginner: prepare a rebase
prompt_templates.scenario: Clean up local commits before review.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me prepare an interactive rebase for my last four local commits. Explain the safe checks and backup steps first.

prompt_templates.title: Intermediate: resolve a conflict
prompt_templates.scenario: Understand a merge conflict before editing.
prompt_templates.prompt: I have a conflict in a configuration file. Help me compare ours and theirs, decide what to keep, and list verification steps.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced: find a regression
prompt_templates.scenario: Locate the commit that introduced a bug.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Git bisect plan for a reproducible regression. Include good and bad revisions, a test command, and recovery steps.

prompt_templates.title: Expert: recover rewritten history
prompt_templates.scenario: Restore work after a mistaken history operation.
prompt_templates.prompt: I rebased and lost a local commit. Give me a reflog-based recovery plan that avoids overwriting current work.

output_examples.input: Prepare my last three commits for a pull request.
output: Review the three commits and choose squash, reword, or reorder actions.
Run tests and inspect the final log before pushing.

output_examples.input: A rebase removed a commit I need.
output: Inspect reflog entries to identify the prior commit.
Create a recovery branch at the selected commit.
Compare recovered work before cherry-picking or merging it.

best_practices: Create a backup branch before rewriting history or deleting branches.
Inspect the working tree and test results before continuing a merge or rebase.
Use force-with-lease and coordinate with collaborators before updating shared history.
anti_patterns: Do not rewrite published shared history without team agreement.
Do not accept ours or theirs blindly without reviewing the conflict.
Do not run cleanup commands until you confirm the active repository and protected branches.

faq.question: Does this skill execute Git commands automatically?
faq.answer: It provides instructions and includes an optional local helper script. Review every command before running it.

faq.question: Can it recover deleted commits?
faq.answer: It explains reflog-based recovery when the relevant Git objects still exist locally.

faq.question: Is interactive rebase safe for shared branches?
faq.answer: Use it carefully. Coordinate before rewriting commits that other people may have based work on.

faq.question: What should I do before deleting branches?
faq.answer: Confirm the repository, protect active branches, and create a backup when the work may be needed.

faq.question: Does it support Windows?
faq.answer: The documentation is broadly useful, but the included helper script requires a Bash-compatible environment.

faq.question: Can it fix every merge conflict?
faq.answer: No. It helps analyze common patterns, but repository context and tests determine the correct resolution.
